rebuttal_or_critique: I find the continued insistence on a 'withdrawal of accommodation' stance increasingly disconnected from the current macroeconomic reality. With core inflation at 3.60%, which is well below our 4.00% target, the real policy rate is already significantly positive. Maintaining a stance of 'withdrawal of accommodation' when the core inflation trajectory is so benign risks overtightening and unnecessarily constraining the 6.80% GVA growth momentum. Food inflation at 8.30% is largely a supply-side phenomenon that monetary policy is ill-equipped to address through further tightening. We must acknowledge that the current repo rate of 6.50% is already restrictive enough to anchor expectations; persisting with a stance that implies further tightening is unwarranted and risks an avoidable slowdown.
